TextView.android:text: Simple explanations of words you may see during practice. A measurement is an estimate from this prototype, not a medical score.

Recording duration: How long the microphone captured the attempt. It does not show how good the attempt was.

Voice activity duration: How long the sound-level algorithm marked audio as active. It may miss quiet voice or include other sounds, so it is only an estimate.

Voice onset: The estimated start of detected sound activity. It is not a direct measurement of vocal-fold movement.

Acoustic intensity: How strong the sound signal is at the microphone. Phone distance and room conditions affect it; it is not a direct measure of vocal effort.

Fundamental frequency (pitch): A signal estimate related to how high or low a voiced sound is. Natural pitch changes are not automatically errors.

Acceleration: A change in movement over time. A neck sensor would measure movement at its own position, not directly see vocal folds.

Signal amplitude: The size of a signal. A larger number does not automatically mean better speaking.

Signal envelope: A smoothed line that shows how a signal rises and falls over time.

Surface EMG: Small electrical signals recorded from muscles beneath skin electrodes. It does not directly measure vocal-fold muscle activity.

EMG envelope: A smoothed summary of how the recorded surface EMG signal changes over time.

Sampling frequency: How many times a device records a signal each second.

Timestamp: A time marker attached to a measurement.

Synchronisation: Lining up measurements from different sources by their timing.

BLE: Bluetooth Low Energy, a short-range wireless method planned for sending wearable data. Wearable data is not connected in this version.

Signal quality: An indication of how usable a recording or measurement appears. Poor quality can make estimates unreliable.

Baseline: A person's earlier measurement used as a comparison when the same exercise and similar conditions are used. It is not a clinical target.

Measurement repeatability: How similar repeated measurements are when the same task is done under similar conditions. Similar numbers do not by themselves mean improvement.
